meta.notes: Solid-state battery manufacturers, Europe, as of February 2026. Source image phase distribution: R&D ×8, Ramp-up ×7, Launched ×2. Individual phase assignments use domain knowledge; open_questions flagged where uncertain. Stage mapping: Launched → commercial, Ramp-up → pilot, R&D → rd.

companies.name: Ilika

open_questions: Confirm current phase — source image shows aggregate phase distribution only; assigned 'pilot/ramp-up' based on domain knowledge

companies.notes: Publicly listed UK solid-state battery company. Develops Stereax microbatteries and Goliath large-format cells. Oxide ceramic electrolyte.

research.summary: Ilika operates two parallel solid-state programs: Stereax (oxide-based microbatteries for medical implants, now in commercial production via Cirtec Medical in the US) and Goliath (large-format cells for EVs and defence). An automated Goliath pilot line was completed in October 2025, achieving a 93% manufacturing success rate on 2Ah and 10Ah cells. Larger 50Ah P2 prototype cells are in development for customer sampling in 2026.

companies.name: LiNa Energy

open_questions: Confirm current phase — source image footnote ¹: sodium-metal chloride battery type

companies.notes: Developing sodium-metal chloride solid-state batteries using NASICON-type ceramic electrolyte. Inherently non-flammable chemistry.

research.summary: LiNa Energy (Lancaster University spin-out, 2017) develops planar solid-state sodium-metal-chloride cells using an ultra-thin NASICON-type ceramic electrolyte, targeting stationary energy storage. The company secured €4M including a €952K Innovate UK grant to build an automated ceramic electrolyte pilot line. A 10 kWh sodium BESS was deployed on the Indian grid; pilot projects are underway in Europe and the Middle East. No confirmed 2025-2026 production-scale milestones have been publicly announced.

companies.name: TaiSan

open_questions: Confirm phase — assigned R&D based on 2022 founding and quasi-solid-state sodium technology stage

companies.notes: Founded Jan 2022 by Sanzhar Taizhan (Forbes 30 Under 30). Quasi-solid-state sodium batteries for automotive. Raised £1.3M pre-seed (EIT InnoEnergy) + £3.2M Series A. Excludes lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper. Compatible with existing Li-ion manufacturing lines.

research.summary: TaiSan (formerly Taisan Motors) develops quasi-solid-state sodium batteries using a proprietary polymer electrolyte with metal anode, targeting automotive applications. The company closed a £3.2M Series A in February 2026, bringing its post-money valuation to ~£12.5M, and has signed MoUs with automotive OEMs in seven countries. The technology claims ~20% cost reduction versus lithium-ion and compatibility with existing Li-ion production lines. Still at R&D/early validation stage with no pilot-line capacity reported.

companies.name: HyET Lithium

open_questions: Solid electrolyte type not specified in source image ('Unknown')
Confirm relationship to HyET Group (hydrogen compression technology)

companies.notes: Spin-off in the HyET Group ecosystem. Electrolyte type listed as Unknown in source image.

research.summary: HyET Lithium (Arnhem, NL; founded 2022) is a spin-off of the HyET Group developing high-energy-density solid-state lithium-ion batteries via roll-to-roll manufacturing with silicon anodes. The electrolyte chemistry is not publicly disclosed. The company is at early R&D/startup stage with no confirmed pilot-line capacity or external funding announcements as of May 2026. Their website claims advantages in safety, energy density, and low-temperature performance.

companies.name: AVESTA (ABEE)

open_questions: Source image shows founded 2023 — this is the Ninove R&D facility opening date; actual company founding is 2019
Confirm whether gigafactory plans in Seneffe (Manage) are still active

companies.notes: Avesta Battery & Energy Engineering (ABEE), part of AVESTA Holding. Ninove R&D facility opened Nov 2023 (€27M, largest SSB upscaling centre in Benelux). Oxide and sulfide solid electrolyte pilot lines. Also announced gigafactory in Seneffe (3 GWh) and battery recycling plant in Dour.

research.summary: AVESTA (formerly ABEE) operates a 9,000 m² R&D and upscaling centre in Ninove (opened Nov 2023) with oxide and sulfide solid electrolyte pilot lines. Generation 0 prototype pouch cells achieved 500 cycles at 82% capacity retention; Generation 1 cells showed only 3% capacity loss in the first 100 cycles. As of January 2025 the company planned independent cell validation and a transition to prismatic cell production by end-2025. A recycling facility capable of processing 20,000 t/year of LFP batteries is scheduled to begin construction mid-2026.

companies.name: SOLiTHOR

products.name: composite solid electrolyte (SCE, silica nanoporous matrix)

open_questions: Confirm current phase — assigned R&D/early pilot based on 2021 founding and publicly known stage

companies.notes: Spin-out from imec (Belgium). Proprietary sol-gel-derived Solid Composite Electrolyte (SCE) with nanoporous silica matrix. Achieved 1,000+ cycles on 3Ah lithium-metal cell. Targets automotive and maritime applications. Headquarters in Sint-Truiden, 65 km from Brussels.

research.summary: SOLiTHOR (imec spin-out, founded Sept 2021) develops solid-state lithium-metal cells using a proprietary sol-gel-derived Solid Composite Electrolyte (SCE) with a nanoporous silica matrix, offering higher energy density and improved manufacturability versus competing oxide and sulfide approaches. The company raised €10M seed funding led by imec.xpand and has demonstrated over 1,000 cycles on a 3Ah lithium-metal cell — a key milestone for aviation and maritime markets. Current stage is R&D with no announced production capacity.

companies.name: BASQUEVOLT
companies.notes: Basque Country solid-state battery startup, spin-off from CIDETEC / CIC energiGUNE. Polymer composite solid electrolyte. Backed by Iberdrola, TotalEnergies, Stellantis and EIT InnoEnergy. A-Sample Line launched 2024 delivering prototype solid-state cells up to 80 Ah to automotive and aviation customers. Commercial production of 10 GWh/year targeted for 2027.

research.summary: BasqueVolt (CIDETEC spin-off, backed by EIT InnoEnergy) launched its A-Sample Line manufacturing facility in 2024, producing prototype solid-state cells up to 80 Ah for automotive and aviation partners. Commercial production of 10 GWh/year is targeted for 2027. A new R&D centre was planned to inaugurate by end-2025. Investment exceeds €700M for the first production line.

companies.name: ENSURGE

open_questions: Source image footnote ²: focus on microbatteries — confirm if larger-format cells are in development

companies.notes: Formerly Thin Film Electronics ASA. Corporate HQ Oslo; R&D and manufacturing in San Jose (US). Solid-state lithium microbatteries via roll-to-roll printing on stainless steel. Delivering commercial shipments to medical device and consumer electronics customers. Source image footnote ²: focus on microbatteries.

research.summary: Ensurge Micropower (Oslo-listed, formerly Thin Film Electronics) produces solid-state lithium microbatteries (1–100 mAh range) via its proprietary roll-to-roll Micro Power Platform, targeting medical devices and portable electronics. In November 2025 the company signed joint development and investment agreements with Corning Incorporated to advance ultra-high-performance solid-state microbattery technology. The company achieved 90% stacking yield in early 2025 and is targeting commercial scale-up in 2026.

companies.name: Qkera

open_questions: Source image shows founded 2024; confirmed founding date is November 2023 (TUM spin-off)

companies.notes: TUM spin-off (Prof. Jennifer Rupp, Dr. Andreas Weis), founded Nov 2023. Ceramic oxide solid electrolyte (1–20 µm) with proprietary bilayer approach. 30–50% higher energy density claimed. Compatible with roll-to-roll manufacturing. Won 2024 Falling Walls competition.

research.summary: Qkera (TUM/MIT spin-off, Garching; founded late 2023) develops a proprietary ceramic-oxide solid electrolyte membrane (1–20 µm) that claims 30–50% higher energy density versus conventional lithium-ion, with a roll-to-roll-compatible manufacturing process. The company secured a seven-figure pre-seed round led by EIT InnoEnergy in late 2025 and is targeting a pilot line by 2026. Qkera is currently in talks with major European OEMs and battery manufacturers, and holds a growing patent family.

companies.name: theion

open_questions: Source image footnote ³: polymer electrolyte integrated within cathode structure — confirm technology status

companies.notes: Berlin-based solid-state startup. Polymer electrolyte integrated within the cathode. Source image footnote ³: within cathode.

research.summary: theion (Berlin, founded 2020) develops lithium-sulfur crystal batteries using its proprietary Direct Crystal Imprinting (DCi) process, which grows a crystalline sulfur cathode directly from molten sulfur without solvents. The cell architecture uses a solid-state polymer electrolyte and a lithium metal anode, targeting energy densities of ≥1,000 Wh/kg primarily for eVTOL and aerospace markets. The company opened a Technology Centre at Berlin-Adlershof with 1 MWh/year of semi-automatic cell assembly capacity for customer samples, and claims third-party validated 2,000-cycle performance for its lithium metal anode chemistry.

companies.name: Blue Solutions

capacities.label: current annual LMP cell production (Ergué-Gabéric + Montréal combined)

products.name: polymer solid electrolyte (LMP — Lithium Metal Polymer)

open_questions: Confirm 25 GWh 2032 target — expansion strategy uses modular ~2.5 GWh gigatowers; scale-up timeline unclear
Third production line being installed at Ergué-Gabéric — confirm capacity addition

companies.notes: Bolloré Group subsidiary. Commercially producing LMP (Lithium Metal Polymer) solid-state batteries. Deployed in Bluebus electric buses and stationary energy storage. Plant in Ergué-Gabéric (near Quimper), Brittany. Combined output ~500 MWh/year across Ergué-Gabéric and Montréal production lines. A third line is being installed at Ergué-Gabéric. One of the two 'Launched' phase companies per source image.

research.summary: Blue Solutions operates two LMP (Lithium-Metal-Polymer) solid-state battery production lines with a combined capacity of ~500 MWh/year — one in Ergué-Gabéric (Brittany) and one in Montréal. A third line is being installed at Ergué-Gabéric. Long-term expansion strategy uses modular ~2.5 GWh 'gigatowers'. The 25 GWh target for 2032 is from the original source image and could not be confirmed from current sources; actual expansion pace is significantly lower. Next-gen GEN4 battery SOP targeted for 2030.

companies.name: ITEN
companies.notes: French solid-state thin-film microbattery maker near Lyon. Commercial production for IoT, medical, and industrial applications. Source image footnote ⁴: thin-film battery. One of the two 'Launched' phase companies per source image.

research.summary: ITEN (Dardilly, near Lyon; founded 2011) commercially produces all-solid-state thin-film microbatteries using an oxide electrolyte, with over 100 customers sampling products for IoT, medical, and industrial connected devices. In April 2025 the company announced a breakthrough 200C discharge rate — 100× higher than conventional Li-ion — for its new Powency product family, qualified for full-scale production in H2 2025. ITEN's Dardilly pilot line produces more than 30 million batteries per year, with a high-volume manufacturing facility planned by 2028.

companies.name: Solvionic

open_questions: Verify classification — Solvionic is primarily an ionic liquid and electrolyte materials developer/supplier, not a cell manufacturer; presence on solid-state manufacturers map may reflect their role as electrolyte partner in EU consortia (SOLiDIFY, EPSILON)

companies.notes: Founded 2003 by François Malbosc. Toulouse-based ionic liquid and solid electrolyte developer. 20 t/year pilot line (2021). €1.4M EPSILON project for solid electrolyte formulations. SOLiDIFY EU consortium partner. Primarily a materials/electrolyte supplier rather than full cell manufacturer.

research.summary: Solvionic (Toulouse, founded 2003) is a specialist ionic liquid and solid/polymer electrolyte materials supplier rather than a full cell manufacturer. The company operates a pilot production line with output increased to 180 kg/month of solid polymer electrolyte as of 2024-2025, and participates in EU battery innovation consortia including SOLiDIFY and the FULL-MAP materials acceleration platform. Solvionic's inclusion on solid-state manufacturer maps reflects its role as an electrolyte partner in EU-funded SSB programs, not direct cell production.

companies.name: ProLogium

open_questions: Original source image showed 16 GWh — revised plan: Fab 1 Phase 1: 0.8 GWh by 2028; Phase 2: 4 GWh by 2030; Phase 3: 12 GWh by 2032
Founded 2006 in Taiwan (Taoyuan City HQ) — record placed under France for European facility

companies.notes: Taiwanese solid-state battery maker (founded 2006, HQ Taoyuan City). Groundbreaking February 2026. Phased build: 0.8 GWh by 2028, 4 GWh by 2030, 12 GWh by 2032, with land reserved for up to 48 GWh long-term. Produces 'Superfluidized All-Inorganic Solid-State' cells (Gen4). Record placed under France for European facility context.

research.summary: ProLogium broke ground on its Dunkirk solid-state battery gigafactory in February 2026. The phased plan calls for Fab 1 Phase 1 completion (0.8 GWh) in 2028, Phase 2 (4 GWh) by 2030, and Phase 3 (12 GWh) by 2032. Land at the Port of Dunkirk has been reserved for future expansion to up to 48 GWh. The previous 16 GWh figure cited in industry trackers has been superseded by this detailed phased roadmap.

companies.name: Swiss Clean Battery

capacities.label: scaling plan 1.2–7.6 GWh — announced but unconfirmed

open_questions: Verify current production status — 2024 production start was announced but not confirmed achieved
Confirm solid electrolyte chemistry under HPB AG license

companies.notes: Swiss Clean Battery AG, founded Feb 2022 in Frauenfeld (Canton Thurgau). Exclusive license from High Performance Battery Technology AG (HPB AG, Teufen). Plans: 1.2–7.6 GWh scaling, 246M CHF investment, production start originally announced 2024.

research.summary: Swiss Clean Battery (Frauenfeld, founded 2022) holds an exclusive license from HPB AG (Teufen) for a solid electrolyte technology that is reportedly manufactured within the cell using existing liquid-electrolyte production processes. Despite announcing production start in 2024 and a CHF 246M investment for a 1.2 GWh phase-1 facility, the company's website as of May 2026 indicates it is still seeking investors and external capital, suggesting the production ramp has not been achieved. The expansion to a full 7.6 GWh gigafactory in Domat-Ems remains contingent on financing.

companies.notes: Italian battery manufacturer founded 1974 in Monterubbiano (FM). Primarily LFP cell production; Teverola 2 gigafactory (8 GWh, LFP) under construction. Inclusion in solid-state manufacturers map is unverified — may reflect a new research program or be a misclassification.

research.summary: Research confirms that FAAM's core business is LFP lithium-ion cell manufacturing, not solid-state batteries. The Monterubbiano site produces lead-acid batteries, while the Teverola facility has a 0.35 GWh LFP cell line with an 8 GWh Teverola 2 gigafactory under construction (>€417M Italian government funding, production starting 2026). No solid-state battery program could be identified in any public source. Inclusion on the solid-state Europe map appears to be a misclassification; stage set to unknown pending any clarifying announcement.

companies.name: GQ energy

open_questions: Electrolyte type not specified in source image ('Unknown') — confirm technology

companies.notes: GQenergy Srl, founded April 2017 in Villa Minozzo (Reggio Emilia). Develops solid-state cells with a proprietary special membrane for stationary and EV energy storage.

research.summary: GQenergy Srl (Villa Minozzo, Reggio Emilia; founded April 2017) is a small Italian startup that patented a solid-state cell design in January 2018 based on a proprietary polymer membrane, claimed to offer small dimensions, high flexibility, and low production costs for applications ranging from small electronics to electric vehicles. The company received a €67K regional innovation grant in 2021. No pilot-scale production, external investment rounds, or 2025-2026 milestones have been publicly announced; the company appears to remain at very early R&D stage.
